This massive discount is further amplified when compared against the sector benchmark, where the company trades at a bargain P/B of 0.42x against a sector benchmark of 1.86x [E7]. The business is undergoing a powerful operational inflection, demonstrated by a stellar compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months of 176% [E15]. This dramatic acceleration in earnings [E57] means profit growth currently exceeds 1-year price growth by 226%, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E46] while trading at the absolute floor of its 52-week range [E5]. This top-line failure underscores a multi-year trend of earnings decay, evidenced by compounded profit growth over five years at -14% and worsening dramatically over three years to -38% [E13, E14]. Furthermore, the business generates an exceptionally weak return on equity of just 1.28%, falling far short of the sector benchmark of 11.49% [E8]. However, the bear's focus on historical earnings decay ignores the dramatic inflection point happening right now, where trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged by 176% [E15]. This sudden acceleration handily crushes the sector median profit growth of 39.6% [E66]. The market is myopically fixated on backward-looking P/E metrics of 32.61x or 40x [E1, E6] while completely ignoring that the stock trades at a deep discount to its net assets with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.51x, or 0.42x against the sector benchmark [E2, E7]. Furthermore, this massive earnings turnaround is actively outpacing the stock price, as recent profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 226% [E46]. Far from being a broken asset, the company is starting to outperform expectations as earnings growth accelerates from its prior trough [E46, E57].
